question.problem: John is traveling in the subway and wants to determine how the subway speed changes as time goes on. What are appropriate units for the rate of change of the speed, in terms of base units?
question.worked_solution:
We *measure the change* in the speed, as *we change* the time. Consequently, any appropriate unit must take the form

$$
\frac{\text{unit of speed}}{\text{unit of time}}.
$$

In terms of meters and seconds, the unit for speed is $\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}},$ and the unit for time is $\text{s}.$ Therefore, the appropriate unit for the rate of change of speed is

$$
\frac{(\frac{\text{m}}{\text{s}})}{\text{s}}=\frac{\text{m}}{{\text{s}}^{2}}.
$$

or, meters per square second.
